title: Time Series Momentum
author: Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen
key_claim: Past 1-12 month return of an asset predicts its own future return across 58 futures; partial reversal at longer horizons.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: basis for strategy 3 (TSMOM).
notes: Results are volatility-scaled diversified futures portfolios, not single unscaled ETFs. See S04/S05 critiques.

title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
author: Hurst, Ooi, Pedersen
key_claim: Diversified 1/3/12-month trend positive in every decade since 1880; positive in most large 60/40 drawdowns; weaker after 2008.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: Medium: supports trend on GLD/SPY/QQQ/TLT but evidence is a 67-market diversified portfolio.
notes: Authors' firm sells trend funds. Pre-1985 data are reconstructed. Abstract-level figures; full PDF could not be parsed.

title: Which Trend Is Your Friend?
author: Levine, Pedersen
key_claim: Time-series momentum and moving-average crossover signals are essentially the same filter in general form.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: strategies 2 and 3 are near-duplicates, so they are correlated tests (matters for multiple-testing).
notes: Publisher's version on author institution repository.

title: Time series momentum: Is it there?
author: Huang, Li, Wang, Zhou
key_claim: Asset-by-asset predictability is weak in and out of sample; TSMOM profits similar to a strategy using historical mean returns.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: warns that single-asset TSMOM edge may be small/illusory.
notes: Critique of S01.

title: Time Series Momentum and Volatility Scaling
author: Kim, Tse, Wald
key_claim: Most TSMOM alpha comes from volatility scaling; unscaled TSMOM is similar to buy-and-hold.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: our TSMOM is unscaled and single-asset, so expect little edge.

title: Is Trend Still Your Friend? A Microstructural Account of the Demise of Short-Term Trend-Following
author: Kurth, Eisler, Rej, Bouchaud
key_claim: Short-term trend profits fell after 2008 in small-tick futures; large-tick contracts held up.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: Medium: evidence of decay of fast trend; our 50-day variant is the fastest.
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Summary from abstract.

title: The Science and Practice of Trend-Following Systems
author: Sepp, Lucic
key_claim: Trend profits come from positive long-horizon autocorrelation; can coexist with short-term mean reversion.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: Low-medium: theory linking trend and mean reversion.
notes: Preprint; discloses generative-AI use. Abstract only.

title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
author: Faber
key_claim: 10-month SMA timing on each asset class gives equity-like returns with lower volatility and drawdowns (1900-2008).
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: basis for proposed strategy P2 and for N=200 day trend.
notes: Backtest; author runs ETFs using related ideas.

title: Swedroe on Faber's 'Revisited 10 Years Later' (JPM 2018)
author: Swedroe (summary of Faber)
key_claim: Faber's 2018 update reports the model held up in real time 2006-2017.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: out-of-sample check of S08.
notes: Summary, not the paper itself.

title: Global Tactical Asset Allocation, automated (replication of Faber 2006-2025)
author: Concretum Group
key_claim: Out of sample 2006-Mar 2025: Sharpe 0.68, CAGR 6.05% vs 0.81 / 11.7% in the original 1972-2005 sample.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: Medium: quantifies post-publication decay.
notes: Third-party blog; numbers not verified. Has a commercial newsletter.

title: Risk Premia Harvesting Through Momentum (summary of Antonacci 2012)
author: Alpha Architect (summary of Antonacci)
key_claim: Absolute (T-bill hurdle) plus relative momentum improves returns and cuts drawdowns vs either alone.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: basis for strategies 5/6 (rotation with cash filter).
notes: Antonacci's book is paid; only legitimate summaries used. The 2017 journal version was found only on an unofficial repository, so it was not used.

title: Global Equity Momentum: A Craftsman's Perspective
author: ReSolve Asset Management (Butler et al.)
key_claim: GEM replicates closely in- and out-of-sample to 2018 but results are highly sensitive to lookback and rebalance date.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: rotation strategies are fragile to parameter choice.
notes: Authors manage money; no post-2018 data.

title: A Comprehensive Look at the Empirical Performance of Moving Average Trading Strategies
author: Zakamulin
key_claim: 155 years: MA rules generate many false signals; outperformance concentrated in bear markets; real-time/out-of-sample performance much weaker than in-sample.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: sets realistic expectations for strategy 2.

title: Leverage for the Long Run
author: Gayed, Bilello
key_claim: S&P 500 1928-2015: 3x daily leveraged buy-and-hold CAGR 15.3%, vol 56.7%, Sharpe 0.21, max DD -99.9%; 3x 200-day-MA rotation CAGR 26.8%, vol 37.3%, Sharpe 0.47, max DD -92.2%. Volatility is much higher below the 200-day MA.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: direct basis for strategy 2 on leveraged ETFs.
notes: Assumes 1% annual fee only (no (L-1) borrowing cost), states 'no cost to execute', single market, in-sample. Authors ran a fund using it. Numbers read from the PDF text.

title: The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
author: Cheng, Madhavan
key_claim: Daily rebalancing creates path dependence; long holding periods erode value in volatile markets; costs and taxes add drag.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: leveraged ETF decay mechanics.
notes: Publisher page; full text needs free registration.

title: Path-Dependence of Leveraged ETF Returns
author: Avellaneda, Zhang
key_claim: Exact formula: leveraged ETF log return = L x underlying log return - (L^2-L)/2 x realized variance - costs; verified on 56 LETFs.
relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: justifies vol-gating (proposal P1) and our synthetic series check.
notes: Author preprint.

author: Moreira, Muir
key_claim: Scaling exposure inversely to recent variance raised Sharpe ratios and alphas for the market and several factors.

notes: Authors from Man Group (practitioners). Summary via abstract.

relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: optional extra check for grid selection.

relevance_to_daily_etf_trading: High: realistic expectations.
